briefs.source_chain: Buffers that absorbed prior oil shocks (US exports, weak Chinese demand, inventories) are fading while supply disruptions converge, shifting MS from a benign de-escalation baseline to an oil risk-premium baseline (45% probability) therefore WTI/Brent and SPR levels signal tightness therefore persistently higher oil delays airfare disinflation and produces second-round inflation effects therefore MS raises core PCE, trims GDP/consumption/investment, trims payrolls and raises unemployment therefore MS now expects two more 25bp hikes (Dec, March) to 4.25-4.50% terminal, citing Warsh's hawkish comments and the neutral-rate revision.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: fading buffers + converging supply disruptions push MS to an oil risk-premium baseline therefore current WTI/Brent/SPR levels therefore delayed airfare disinflation and second-round effects therefore raised core PCE / trimmed GDP, consumption, investment, payrolls, raised unemployment therefore two more 25bp hikes to 4.25-4.50% terminal, citing Warsh and the neutral-rate revision, with the baseline assigned 45% probability.

briefs.source_chain: FOMC hikes 25bp to 3.75-4% unanimously and drops the supply-shock inflation framing therefore SEP shows GDP up, unemployment down to 4.1% (below the 4.2% long-run estimate), core PCE 2026 up to 3.4%, most members seeing upside inflation risk and none seeing downside employment risk therefore SG reads lower perceived stagflation risk and a Committee focus squarely on inflation therefore 2026 dots imply 50bp more this year (12/19 aligned), 2027 dots split (four favoring ~2 cuts vs eight favoring a third hike), long-run dot at 3.2% therefore, combined with Warsh calling policy not-yet-restrictive and the hike a removal of accommodation, SG keeps its call for two more 25bp hikes (Dec, March, 75bp total) to unwind the 2025 insurance cuts, conditional on inflation data not disappointing.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain, same figures and same conditional call for two more 25bp hikes (75bp total) framed as unwinding the 2025 insurance cuts, contingent on inflation data.

distortions.what: Brief renders the 2027 dot split as "four cutters versus eight hikers"; source specifies the four project "at least two 25bp cuts," not just any cut.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the directional split (dovish minority vs. hawkish majority) and the 2027 disagreement read are unchanged; only the magnitude qualifier on the dovish four is dropped.

briefs.source_chain: Fed hikes 25bp to 3.75-4.0% as expected therefore three hawkish signals (removing-accommodation framing implying policy not yet restrictive, geopolitics/oil newly cited as a reaction-function driver, neutral rate revised up to 3.25% from 3.06%) therefore MS moves from an expected 50bp of total tightening (Sept+Dec) entering the meeting to 75bp total, adding a March hike, for a 4.25-4.50% terminal in 1Q27 therefore an October hike cannot be ruled out given elevated pricing, but de-escalation or faster disinflation could cap it at one more hike in December therefore Rates, FX, MBS and Munis desks each position around this hawkish read.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: two more 25bp hikes (Dec, March) to 4.25-4.5% terminal in 1Q27, up from a prior 50bp-total view entering the meeting; same three hawkish signals; same October-hike-not-ruled-out / de-escalation-caps-it-at-December two-sided risk; same four desks (Rates, FX, MBS, Munis) attaching trade ideas.

distortions.what: Brief says MBS and Munis desks "attach trade ideas" to the hawkish read; source gives Rates and FX explicit "Trade idea:" bullets, while MBS states a directional bias (long basis on weakness) and Munis states a neutral/barbell preference without a formal "Trade idea:" line.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — all four desks do state a directional stance in the source, so the brief's summary framing doesn't add a position that isn't there or misstate any single desk's actual call.

briefs.source_chain: DM equity buying was funded by Asia selling therefore US equities saw the largest net buying in 5 weeks led by Tech (previously flagged light vs. Asia), Mag-7 inflows pushed allocations back near peak with Software the most net-bought sub-sector, and Europe was net bought at the fastest pace in 5 months (short covers, Industrials/Tech/Discretionary) though still near 5-year trough allocations therefore, citing Oppenheimer, GS stays constructive medium-term on equities since compute demand outstripping supply lowers earnings-bubble risk, with SPX EPS growth of 11% penciled for both 2027 ($415) and 2028 ($460); separately, Chinese exports enter at a 30% discount then reprice higher in most sectors, implying ex-China share rising from 18% to 31% by 2035 (largely unpriced, esp. in Latecomer categories); separately, 42 India AI-infrastructure names (+60% YTD vs. NIFTY -11%) drive ~40% of NIFTY 500 capex growth this year.
briefs.brief_chain: Same three-part chain (HF flows, China's Go Global, India AI enablers) with the same figures: 5-week US buying led by Tech, Mag-7 near peak, Software top sub-sector, Europe fastest pace in 5 months on short covers, constructive medium-term equity view per Oppenheimer with the compute-outstrips-supply rationale, 11% SPX EPS growth to $415/$460, 30% discount/7-of-11-sector repricing, 18%-to-31%-by-2035 share, 42 India names at +60% YTD vs. NIFTY -11% driving ~40% of NIFTY 500 capex growth.

distortions.what: Brief omits the SPX EPS 2Q/trailing growth figures (50% YoY, 26% 4-quarter trailing) and the 'over-earning, not a bubble' framing, and omits the MTD Asia HF rotation detail (Korea/Taiwan/Japan to HK/China; China/India positioning jump) and the named Latecomer sub-sectors (robotaxis, surgical robots, etc.).
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — these are supporting/secondary data points and examples; the constructive-equity stance, EPS forecast, and China/India theses are unchanged without them.
